1. What this path is for#

CALIBER deliberately separates candidate generation, review, and live apply. That is true for prompts, workflows, and other governed assets even though each asset family has different semantics.

What Apply does#

Apply is POST /jobs/{job_id}/apply (SDK jobs.apply(job_id), and the Apply button in the page). It is the explicit human decision, and these are its rules:

  • Who may. The caller needs caliber.operator and, for a job whose target belongs to a project, owner or editor. A person outside the project gets 404 and a member with another role gets 403, before anything is claimed. There is no second approver: the approval record Apply creates (already approved, naming the caller) is an audit and rollback anchor, not a vote.
  • Which jobs. Only a job at candidate_ready. Any other status answers 409.
  • Intent first. The claim (candidate_ready to applying) and the approval record are committed before the promotion runs. If the promotion fails before any release operation exists, the job returns to candidate_ready and the approval record is withdrawn, so you can retry. If a release operation does exist, the job stays applying until the release reconciler settles it.
  • Simulated releases say so. The response carries simulated, which is true when the promoter is the fake one, and the audit rows record it.
  • Sending it back. POST /jobs/{job_id}/request-changes returns a candidate_ready job to the candidate stage with your notes. It needs owner, editor or reviewer.

Release-candidate signoff and Workspace releases#

These two areas are off by default. Enable them with CALIBER_FEATURE_RELEASE_CANDIDATES=true and restart CALIBER; turning the flag on means you accept their alpha behavior, below.

AreaRoutes it gatesWhat it does in this build
Release-candidate signoff (record-only)/releases/candidates* and /releases/report-jobs*, and the candidate section of the Releases pageAssembles criteria, evidence and waivers, computes a readiness score on the server, and records a go or no-go signoff with a rationale. A signoff records a decision and deploys or rolls back nothing. A waiver's expires_at is honoured every time the candidate is evaluated (a lapsed waiver stops clearing its blocker), and a signed candidate cannot be evaluated, waived or signed again. Scores and evidence references are entered by people: CALIBER does not read them from Evaluations or check that the artifact exists
Workspace releases (experimental)/projects/{id}/releases* (and caliberctl workspace release)The default-off owner worker executes a complete release-local pinned evaluation when explicitly enabled; incomplete plans fail closed. Per-example evidence and expired-attempt recovery are implemented; governed apply remains a later Beta slice

While the flag is off, a call to any of those routes answers HTTP 404 with reason_code: feature_disabled, and the Releases page shows only the live board, the timeline and release operations. Those are core and not behind the flag, and neither are GET /releases/live, GET /releases/timeline and GET /releases/operations. GET /capabilities reports the flag as features.release_candidates, so a client can check it first. The path that governs a release end to end is Apply and rollback, above.
